text:
Dylan Samberg is the Winnipeg defenseman the box score undersells. He plays 22 minutes a night and the Jets control 57% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him on, more than 15 points better than without him. Winnipeg went eight and two over his last ten games.

His job is defense, and he does it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 21% of the entries aimed at him last season (typical is 11%), and Evolving-Hockey put him in the 95th percentile at taking chances away. He skates well, too: 97th percentile for top speed by the NHL's EDGE tracking, with a 95.7 mph shot.

The scoring is running hot. He has 12 points in 26 games, including a four-game assist streak, and his points pace sits above our talent range of 0.65 to 1.07 per 60. He's shooting 10% against a usual 5.5%.

What's real is the part that matters most for the Jets: the ice tilts when he's out there.
headline: Samberg tilts the ice for Winnipeg
